options.why: Relative velocity is $v_B-v_A=(-22)-(+20)=-42\text{ m/s}$, whose magnitude is $42\text{ m/s}$ when the cars move in opposite directions.

options.text: Car B approaches at $2\text{ m/s}$, because speeds are subtracted when two objects move in opposite directions.
options.why: Subtracts the speeds, which is correct only for objects moving in the same direction.

options.text: Car B approaches at $22\text{ m/s}$, because the faster of the two cars sets the speed at which they close.
options.why: Lets the faster car alone set the closing speed instead of combining the two velocities.

options.text: Car B approaches at $22\text{ m/s}$, because the speed of an object is the same for every observer.
options.why: Treats speed as independent of the observer, but velocity is measured relative to a frame of reference.

options.why: A greater acceleration over a shorter distance gives the same speed, since $v^2=2aL$ with $a=gh/L$ gives $v^2=2gh$ for both.

options.text: The block on ramp 2 is faster, because it travels the greater distance and so gains more speed.
options.why: Overlooks the smaller acceleration on the longer ramp; the speed depends on the height only.

options.why: Treats equal work as equal power, forgetting that power is the rate at which the work is done.
